title: Managing the commons: a simple model of the emergence of institutions through collective action
publisher: International Journal of the Commons (Ubiquity Press)

key_points.claim: Bravo presents a NetLogo ABM that replicates institutional emergence in common-pool resource (CPR) problems. Institutions and agent strategies are both modelled with the ADICO grammar.
key_points.evidence_quote: We used the ADICO grammar of institutions as the basic structure to model both agents’ strategies and institutions.

key_points.claim: Institutions emerge without agents having advanced cognition. Imitation plus random exploration is enough, provided collective-choice arrangements exist.
key_points.evidence_quote: simple micro-level behavioural mechanisms (imitation+random exploration of the strategy space) represent a sufficient condition to promote well adapted institutional arrangements leading to a sustainable management of the commons

key_points.claim: Agents can emerge institutions that improve both resource stock and agent energy. OLS regressions on simulation output show this effect holds when the other parameters are controlled for.
key_points.evidence_quote: The introduction of the institution positively affects both the amount of resource in the system and agents’ energy.

key_points.claim: The harder it is for agents to change their institution (longer emergence time, higher change threshold), the worse the outcomes. The paper links this to Ostrom's collective-choice design principle.
key_points.evidence_quote: both the institutional emergence time and the proportion of agents needed to change the institution negatively affect both indicators

key_points.claim: The paper reviews earlier CPR ABMs, e.g. Deadman et al. 2000, Jager & Janssen 2003, Janssen & Ostrom 2006 and Smajgl et al. 2008. It differs from Smajgl et al. by aggregating agents' beliefs into rules, using cognitively simpler agents, and modelling resource dynamics with bio-economic models.
key_points.evidence_quote: Smajgl et al. (2008) were the first to apply the ADICO framework to model rule changes in resource dilemmas.

key_points.claim: ABMs are argued to complement lab and field studies by allowing flexible virtual experiments and long-term dynamics. The planned research programme is to add cheating and sanctioning, validate against real CPR data, and apply the model to specific cases.
key_points.evidence_quote: they allow to design virtual experiments using a more flexible set of conditions than what is feasible in the lab and to analyse their long term dynamics more easily than what is possible in the field

key_points.claim: Agents adapted institutions to resource availability. For example, they chose rules that let them harvest only at long intervals, which resembles discussions in CPR lab experiments.
key_points.evidence_quote: agents selected institutions allowing them to harvest only at distant intervals of time

reliability_notes: Full text was available. The article is open access and peer-reviewed. The model is explicitly preliminary and highly abstract, and it has not been validated against empirical data.
